note: Offline, no model or SAM call: every number is read from the stored runs. Muse Spark's observe step (subject, free-motion window, reference object, world, slow-motion, spoken facts, experiment type) is compared with the renders' exact truth (bench/synth/clips) and, for the four clips that are not renders, with facts checked by hand. Judgement calls: (1) subject matching is lenient on kind (a block may be a box or mass, a puck a disc, a bob a ball) and on colour words (off-white is white), but it needs a colour and a kind; for pendulum bobs the colour comes from the render's RGB. (2) The free-motion window is release to impact, landing, the stopper, the last converged bounce, or the end of the clip for pendulums and springs, from the truth's event times times the slow-motion factor; before release a bob or block is held, so a window that starts at 0 loses some IoU. (3) A reference counts as picked when it is present and names the right kind of object (stick, bar or ruler; paper or sheet), and the length is right within 5%. (4) Slow motion is scored only when the clip itself states it, and none of the renders draws or speaks a caption (the factor is in their metadata), so the stated count is zero; the slowed clips are listed instead, with the clock check's reading. (5) On four showcase clips we gave the subject and/or the ruler with the clip (moon-jump, moon-jump-slowed, sample-pendulum; the metre stick on hardening-spring), so those fields are the hint, not the observer, and are left out of the subject and ruler counts. (6) Six showcase renders are matched to their bench clips by size, fps, length, scale and the constants in the credit text (the web copies are re-encoded, so the bytes differ). (7) hindi-pendulum has no physical ruler read from the picture; its scale is the narrated string, so it is scored under narration facts, not under the ruler. (8) The naive default's trouble is judged from the physics (a gravity scale needs the right g, an unslowed clip and no drag), not re-run; whether SAM would find “the moving object” by that name was not tested. A reason is hard when the observer's answer is right and the naive default's is not, shared when both miss, soft when it is a degradation rather than a failure.
